svg.title: Four-Week Cargo Claims Readiness Plan
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-08-claims-readiness-roadmap; chapter number: 12; title: Four-Week Cargo Claims Readiness Plan; subtitle: Evidence, coverage proof, high-value protocol and claim filing; chart type: timeline_roadmap; caption: Brokers sit outside Carmack and contingent cargo only matches what the carrier carries; Peerless saw one $17,000 contingent payout in 45 years. Documents win claims.; assumptions note: The weekly sequence is an editorial rollout. Clocks, tracker prices and payout figures are attributed practitioner claims.; note: Sources - Freight 360 (qTcDOmwZMjI), LOGISTICS RISK EXPERT by Cassandra Gaines (Ig6sI3O1a14), CargoRex with Jared Palmer (xQYjaYAvyms) and Cargo Rant (NxIispBOkz8).; weeks: week: Week 1; title: Build the claim file first; deliverable: Standing folder per load with bill of lading, commercial invoice, packing list, photos and every carrier email.; gate: No load closes without its evidence file started.; week: Week 2; title: Prove coverage in writing; deliverable: Certificates pulled through Highway, RMIS or AssureAssist as holder; carrier's insurance agent emails confirmation that the commodity is not excluded.; gate: A carrier's verbal yes does not count.; week: Week 3; title: Lock the high-value protocol; deliverable: High-value loads go only to relationship carriers, never a load board, with a covert tracker now about $15 instead of $750.; gate: Theft response begins inside the 24 to 48 hour window.; week: Week 4; title: Standardize claim filing; deliverable: Formal written claim with a dollar amount and commercial invoice, tracked against the 30-day acknowledgment and 120-day disposition clocks.; gate: Check contracts for a specific nine-month limit before accepting 'too old'.
